## Classes

### <a name="nagios"></a>`nagios`

The class installs the Nagios, NRPE and plugin packages, renders nagios.cfg,
cgi.cfg and resource.cfg, and declares one nagios::collect_type per object
type so that fragments exported by nagios::type::* resources on monitored
nodes are assembled into conf.d/nagios_<type>.cfg.

Paths and package names default to module Hiera data (data/os/*.yaml). The
nagios::type::* defines resolve the same keys through lookup(), so override
them in Hiera rather than with a resource-like class declaration to keep the
server and its clients consistent.

#### Examples

##### A monitoring server collecting objects targeted at it

```puppet
class { 'nagios':
  server_name => 'monitoring1',
}
include nagios::defaults
```

### <a name="nagios--collect_type"></a>`nagios::collect_type`

Declared by class nagios for every object type. With exported set, the
concat::fragment resources exported by nagios::type::* on other nodes and
tagged for this server are collected into the file.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `nagios::collect_type` defined type:

Directory receiving nagios_<name>.cfg, defaults to conf.d
under the configured cfg_dir.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-nagios--collect_type--server_name"></a>`server_name`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

Collect fragments tagged for this server instead of the
fragments exported without a server name.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-nagios--collect_type--exported"></a>`exported`

Data type: `Boolean`

Whether to collect exported fragments at all.

Default value: `true`

### <a name="nagios--service--http"></a>`nagios::service::http`

Depending on ssl_mode the define exports up to three nagios::type::service
resources for the current node, all relying on the commands declared by
nagios::command::http on the server:

| ssl_mode | http content | https content | certificate | http redirect |
|----------|--------------|---------------|-------------|---------------|
| `false`  | yes          |               |             |               |
| `true`   | yes          | yes           | check_cert  |               |
| `force`  |              | yes           | check_cert  | yes           |
| `only`   |              | yes           | check_cert  |               |

The credentials given with use_auth end up in clear text in the exported
fragment, in PuppetDB and in the Nagios configuration file, as Nagios needs
them. Passing auth_password as Sensitive only keeps it out of the catalog,
report and logs of the monitored node.

#### Examples

##### Check that a site answers over https and redirects http to it

```puppet
nagios::service::http { 'www.example.org':
  ssl_mode     => 'force',
  check_string => 'Welcome',
  server_names => ['monitoring1'],
}
```

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `nagios::service::http` defined type:

* [`check_domain`](#-nagios--service--http--check_domain)
* [`check_url`](#-nagios--service--http--check_url)
* [`check_string`](#-nagios--service--http--check_string)
* [`use`](#-nagios--service--http--use)
* [`port`](#-nagios--service--http--port)
* [`ssl_mode`](#-nagios--service--http--ssl_mode)
* [`use_auth`](#-nagios--service--http--use_auth)
* [`check_cert`](#-nagios--service--http--check_cert)
* [`auth_name`](#-nagios--service--http--auth_name)

* [`redirect_status`](#-nagios--service--http--redirect_status)
* [`redirect_code`](#-nagios--service--http--redirect_code)
* [`server_names`](#-nagios--service--http--server_names)

### <a name="nagios--type--service"></a>`nagios::type::service`

With use_nrpe the check command is wrapped into one of the check_nrpe
commands declared by nagios::command::nrpe_timeout and
nagios::command::nrpe_host, which the server must include.

#### Examples

##### An NRPE check with arguments against the current node

```puppet
nagios::type::service { 'load':
  host_name     => $facts['networking']['fqdn'],
  use_nrpe      => true,
  check_command => 'check_load',
  nrpe_args     => '-w 5,4,3 -c 10,8,6',
  server_names  => ['monitoring1'],
}
```

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `nagios::type::service` defined type:

## Functions

### <a name="nagios--directives"></a>`nagios::directives`

Type: Puppet Language

Entries whose value is undef or an empty array are dropped, arrays are
joined with commas, booleans become 1/0 and every other value is
stringified. Insertion order is preserved.

#### `nagios::directives(Hash[String[1], Any] $directives)`

Entries whose value is undef or an empty array are dropped, arrays are
joined with commas, booleans become 1/0 and every other value is
stringified. Insertion order is preserved.

Returns: `Hash[String[1], String]` Directives ready to be rendered.

##### `directives`

Data type: `Hash[String[1], Any]`

Raw directives as built by the nagios::type::* defines.

### <a name="nagios--object"></a>`nagios::object`

Type: Puppet Language

Renders one Nagios object definition.

#### `nagios::object(String[1] $type, Hash[String[1], Any] $directives)`

The nagios::object function.

Returns: `String` The `define <type> { ... }` block.

##### `type`

Data type: `String[1]`

Nagios object type, for example `host` or `service`.

##### `directives`

Data type: `Hash[String[1], Any]`

Directives of the object, see nagios::directives for the
normalisation applied.

### <a name="nagios--tags"></a>`nagios::tags`

Type: Puppet Language

Builds the tags used to route exported fragments to Nagios servers.

#### `nagios::tags(String[1] $type, Array[String[1]] $server_names)`

The nagios::tags function.

Returns: `Array[String[1]]` The tags to set on the exported fragment.

##### `type`

Data type: `String[1]`

Collected type name as used by nagios::collect_type.

##### `server_names`

Data type: `Array[String[1]]`

Nagios servers the fragment is meant for. When empty the
fragment is tagged for servers declared without a server_name.

## Data types

### <a name="Nagios--Flag"></a>`Nagios::Flag`

A Nagios 0/1 directive, also accepting booleans.

Alias of `Variant[Boolean, Integer[0, 1], Enum['0', '1']]`

### <a name="Nagios--Interval"></a>`Nagios::Interval`

A non negative Nagios interval, attempt count or timeout.

Alias of `Variant[Numeric, Pattern[/\A\d+(\.\d+)?\z/]]`

### <a name="Nagios--Port"></a>`Nagios::Port`

A TCP port, as an integer or a numeric string.

Alias of `Variant[Stdlib::Port, Pattern[/\A\d{1,5}\z/]]`

### <a name="Nagios--ServerNames"></a>`Nagios::ServerNames`

Names of the Nagios servers an exported object is meant for.

Alias of `Array[String[1]]`

### <a name="Nagios--SslMode"></a>`Nagios::SslMode`

- `false`: check http only
- `true`: check http and https
- `force`: check https and that http redirects to https
- `only`: check https only

Alias of `Variant[Boolean, Enum['force', 'only']]`
